p: Autonomous coding Agents can reason, call tools, execute commands, and change files. A basic Agent can be created quickly, but operating it responsibly requires infrastructure around the model. This challenge asks you to build one focused piece of that infrastructure.
blockquote: The Starter Kit works, but it is insecure, hard to diagnose, and only weakly isolated. Choose one middleware problem and make that layer demonstrably better.

td.p: Second- and third-year undergraduates with basic Web/backend experience.
Three days. Team size follows the event-wide rules.
A functional browser UI, Node.js control plane, Agent CRUD, Playground, one-line local Codex Runtime, Ark model connection, and optional ECS deployment.
Implement Trace and Audit, Identity and Authorization, or Safety and Sandboxing.
A three-minute live demo proves the selected middleware changes a real Agent run.

ul.li: Identify a trust, visibility, or isolation boundary in an Agent system.
Design a small middleware contract and integrate it end to end.
Demonstrate both a normal case and a meaningful failure or denial case.
Explain trade-offs and known limitations without pretending the POC is production-ready.

callout.p: Important: a narrow feature that works end to end scores higher than three incomplete middleware ideas.
